items.note: Samarangana-sutradhara rules (as summarised here) for settling Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, artisans and ascetics in particular quarters of a town; background for Paramara-period urban formation.
Prescription that a Shiva temple be set up outside the town in the east and a cremation-ground in the south.
Prescribed placement of market-streets and of craftsmen, weavers, leather-workers and goldsmiths in a Paramara-period town plan; general background on markets and crafts.
Prescription that a deity's temple face east or west, not north or south.
Prescribed town-quarter placement of temples of Vishnu, Surya, the Mothers, Shiva and others.
Three moats of stone or brick to be made around the town and filled with water.
Rampart (vapra) built outside the ring-road, with three moats, from the moat's earth.
Prescribed rampart width (12, 10 or 8 cubits) and height (17, 15 or 13 cubits), narrowing by two angulas per cubit.
Only in an auspicious town are the royal building, sabha, court and other buildings laid out; Yukti-kalpataru also discusses town-layout.
Assessment that Bhoj's Samarangana-sutradhara and Yukti-kalpataru gave chief attention to air, water, health, trade and security in town-planning.

items.note: Bhojshala at Dhara: Prakrit-Sanskrit poems and plays and grammar-diagrams such as the nagabandha are engraved there.
Dhara described as Bhoj's model of town-layout; 24 markets; well-ordered town-planning.
Vidisha famous in tradition and literature; Malavikagnimitra tells the story of Shunga-era palaces of Vidisha.
Paramara-era remains of moat, rampart, temples and structures at Vidisha; the town later razed by invaders.
Vidisha as a trade centre on the sartha-patha routes from Shravasti through Kaushambi to Avanti, toward Mathura and Vidarbha.
Name Besnagar derived from Vaidisha-nagara on the Vidisha (Bes) river; the settlement centre later shifted north of the Betwa.
Paramara-era Vidisha: Bhailasvamidevapura (Bhelsa), Bhailasvami temple and a sun hymn by Chhittapa, poet patronized by Bhoj.
Bhailasvamidevapura kept Vidisha's tradition unbroken from the 9th to 12th century; a prosperous Jain and Vedic centre with temples razed according to Muslim historians.
The Bijamandal mosque must once have been a vast temple later converted to a mosque.
Paramara-era part of Vidisha named Bhailasvamidevapura; Bhoj-patronized poet Chhittapa composed a sun hymn.
At Burhi Mandav, 'the art here resembles the stone-craft of Udayeshvar'.

Paramara-era bastions were square only; round bastions began after Babur for protection from cannonballs.
Parallel north-south and east-west paths and crossroads called a distinctive feature of Paramara-era town-system.

items.note: According to the Udaipur Prashasti, Vairisimha alias Vajratasvami named the town Dhara in memory of his valour.
Dhara the hereditary capital in Sindhuraja's time; Bhoj gave it the glory of the chief capital.
Scholarly assemblies at the Sarasvati-kanthabharana presided over by Bhoj, with scholars receiving honour and financial benefit.
Building described as a library of stone-inscribed works, including Madana's Parijata-manjari engraved there.
Bhoj's own Shringara-manjari-katha describes Dhara; the account is basically traditional yet some facts can be found.
